title: Retargeting audience definitions (Lifecycle Growth Sprint) — draft
content:
Last updated: 2026-01-29 (for retargeting launch checklist)
Owner: Tyler (Mops/attribution)

Context
- Goal: Improve self-serve activation + early retention for Hosted API by retargeting users who have shown intent but haven’t hit activation milestones.
- This doc defines: audiences, inclusion/exclusion logic, lookback windows, platform mapping, and how we suppress enterprise/active sales opps.
- Guardrails:
  - Do NOT target active enterprise opportunities or accounts flagged “no ads” / sensitive.
  - Conservative use of 1P data; comply w/ lifecycle data handling note + GDPR/CAN-SPAM.
  - Ensure attribution hygiene via UTMs and clean audience naming.

Data sources (what we can use)
- Web events (pixel): page views, pricing/enterprise page views, docs/quickstart views, signup conversion.
- Product events (server-side): signup, API key created, first successful request, first 100k tokens, last API request timestamp.
- CRM (HubSpot/Salesforce mirror): active opps, lifecycle stage, account owner, suppression flags.

Key definitions (used across audiences)
- “Signup”: created a Redwood account (user_id assigned).
- “Activation milestone 1”: first successful request (any model) from user_id.
- “Activation milestone 2”: first 100k tokens within 7 days of signup.
- “Return usage”: at least 1 successful request on a day after the activation day.
- “Active opp” (suppression): company has open opportunity in CRM OR has lifecycle stage in {SQL, Opportunity, Negotiation, Security Review} OR account flagged by Sales as “do not market/ads”.

Identity & matching notes
- Primary: hashed email (SHA-256 lowercased trimmed) for Customer Match / Matched Audiences where allowed.
- Secondary: pixel-based website audiences (cookies) for anonymous pre-signup and “signup-no-activation” if user later visits web.
- Region: where possible, restrict EU retargeting to cookie-consented users only.

Global suppression rules (apply to ALL audiences)
1) Active enterprise opp suppression (hard)
- Exclude if CRM indicates ANY of:
  - open opportunity
  - lifecycle stage: SQL+ (SQL, Opportunity, Negotiation/Review)
  - “Security review in progress” checkbox = true
  - Sales-owned account (owner exists AND tier=Enterprise)
- Source of truth: nightly synced list maintained by Isabelle (CRM ops) + weekly review with Jordan.

2) Domain / company-level suppression (hard)
- Exclude if email domain matches:
  - known enterprise/prospect domains in the “Enterprise Exclusion List”
  - regulated/high-sensitivity accounts flagged by privacy/compliance (FinServ/Health) requiring restricted tracking
- Also exclude if company is tagged “Partner-led” campaign to avoid mixed attribution (see partnerships thread).

3) Internal + existing customers suppression (hard)
- Exclude Redwood employees, contractors, and test accounts.
- Exclude users on Dedicated/Private contracts (we do not want to drive them into self-serve ads).

4) Frequency & annoyance guardrails (soft)
- Cap frequency by platform: see “Caps” section.
- Exclude if user has opted out of marketing within last 30 days (where platforms support list-based suppression).

Audience set (draft)

Naming convention
- [Channel]-[Geo]-[FunnelStage]-[Window]-[ExclusionVersion]
- Example: LI-NA-SignupNoActivation-14d-ExclV3

Table: core audiences

A1) Website visitors — Docs/Quickstart intent
- Purpose: capture anonymous devs with intent; drive to quickstart + “first request” snippet.
- Inclusion (pixel):
  - Viewed /docs/* OR /quickstart* OR /sdk/* pages
  - AND spent > 30s OR 2+ page views in session (if available)
- Exclusions:
  - Exclude /careers, /legal, /privacy-only visits
  - Exclude existing signup (if we can match)
  - Exclude active opps via list-based suppression (email match only; pixel-only users cannot be suppressed reliably)
- Lookback window: 30 days
- Geo: NA + UK + EU (EU only if cookie consent is recorded)
- Landing page: hosted api quickstart (aligned w/ PR-412 snippet)

A2) Website visitors — Pricing / Enterprise intent (CAUTION)
- Purpose: limited test; avoid stepping on sales.
- Inclusion (pixel):
  - Viewed /pricing OR /enterprise OR /security OR /compliance
- Exclusions (strict):
  - Exclude all accounts w/ any CRM match (customer match list): if email known and company in CRM, suppress entirely
  - Exclude “high intent” enterprise visitors if we detect >2 enterprise page views (avoid harassment)
- Lookback: 14 days
- Notes: Only run if Sales signs off; may pause if complaints.

A3) Signup but no activation (primary)
- Purpose: biggest conversion lever; nudge to API key + first request.
- Inclusion (server-side list):
  - signup_date within last 30 days
  - AND no first_successful_request
- Sub-segments (for creative + landing):
  - A3a: No API key created
  - A3b: API key created but no first request
- Exclusions:
  - active opp suppression
  - opted out of marketing
  - bounced/invalid emails (if present in suppression lists)
- Lookback: 30 days (membership ends at activation)
- Primary KPI: activation milestone 1 lift within 7 days of first ad impression

A4) Activated but no return
- Purpose: early retention; push “next best action” (streaming, evals, usage dashboard).
- Inclusion (server-side list):
  - first_successful_request occurred
  - AND last_successful_request_at <= (today - 7 days)
  - AND signup_date within last 60 days
- Exclusions:
  - active opp suppression
  - users who hit “first 100k tokens” AND are currently active (avoid wasting spend)
- Lookback: 60 days; exit if they return (any successful request)
- Notes: keep messaging more educational (“ship to prod faster”) vs aggressive upgrade

A5) Activated + hit 100k tokens but stalled (high-value nudge)
- Purpose: recover high-intent users who got traction but stopped.
- Inclusion:
  - hit_100k_tokens = true
  - AND last_successful_request_at <= (today - 14 days)
  - AND signup_date within last 90 days
- Exclusions:
  - active opp suppression
  - accounts that have an assigned CSM (avoid channel conflict)
- Lookback: 90 days
- Note: small audience, higher CPA ok, measure downstream “return usage” and “upgrade intent” signals.

A6) Product evaluators (console visitors) who never generated tokens
- Purpose: reach users who created an account, clicked around console, but didn’t run inference.
- Inclusion:
  - logged into console at least 1 time
  - AND no successful requests
  - AND signup_date within 21 days
- Exclusions:
  - active opp suppression
- Lookback: 21 days

A7) “Cold” prior site visitors (broad) — optional
- Purpose: top-of-funnel fill if volume is too low in other sets.
- Inclusion:
  - Any site visitor
- Exclusions:
  - exclude /careers and /legal
- Lookback: 60 days
- Notes: use only if needed; expect lower performance.

Platform mapping + feasibility

1) Google Ads
- Use:
  - A1, A2, A7 via website remarketing lists.
  - A3-A6 only if we can upload customer match lists (email). Confirm policy compliance + minimum list sizes.
- Notes:
  - Customer Match requires consent and minimum threshold; keep as secondary channel if list sizes are low.

2) LinkedIn
- Use:
  - A3-A6 via Matched Audiences (email list upload) + website retargeting.
  - A1 via website retargeting.
- Pros:
  - Strong for B2B dev audience; good control.
- Cons:
  - More expensive; need tight frequency caps.

3) X/Twitter (optional)
- Use:
  - Pixel retargeting for A1/A7; list-based for A3+ if supported.
- Notes:
  - Attribution noisier; only run if we need incremental reach.

4) Reddit (optional)
- Use:
  - Pixel retargeting A1/A7 (developer audience fit)
- Notes:
  - Keep creative strictly developer-first; avoid enterprise positioning.

Lookback windows & recency tiers (recommended)
- 0–7 days: high recency; aggressive CTA to run first request
- 8–14 days: medium; add reassurance (latency/cost/reliability) + quickstart snippet
- 15–30 days: low; use “new updates” angle + example app template

Budget weighting (initial suggestion)
- A3 Signup-no-activation: 50%
- A4 Activated-no-return: 20%
- A1 Docs/Quickstart visitors: 20%
- A5 100k-stalled: 10%
- A2/A7: 0% initially (enable only if approved)

Frequency caps (starting point)
- LinkedIn: 3 impressions/user/day; 20 impressions/user/7d
- Google Display: 2/day; 14/7d
- X/Reddit: 2/day; 14/7d

Suppression mechanics (how we implement)
- Daily job exports:
  1) Eligible audiences A3-A6 to CSV (hashed emails + audience name)
  2) Suppression list CSV:
     - active opps
     - enterprise exclusion list
     - do-not-ad list
- Upload cadence:
  - Daily for A3 and A6 (fast moving)
  - 2x/week for A4/A5
- Owner: Tyler
- Approval: Jordan/Isabelle for suppression list logic

Edge cases / open questions
- EU consent handling: do we have a reliable “ad_consent=true” flag tied to user_id for list uploads? If not, we should exclude EU from list-based retargeting and only run pixel audiences where consent is recorded.
- Anonymous visitors who later sign up and become active opp: pixel audiences can’t reliably suppress. Mitigation: do not run A2 broadly; keep A1/A7 messaging generic and low-frequency.
- Company-level vs user-level suppression: we should suppress at company domain level when possible to avoid targeting anyone at an enterprise account.
- Minimum audience sizes (platform thresholds): validate list size projections before committing spend.

QA checklist before launch
- [ ] Validate exclusion list is applied in each platform (test with known suppressed emails)
- [ ] Ensure audience names match UTM campaign names
- [ ] Verify no overlap where “activated” users are still in “signup-no-activation” list (dedupe)
- [ ] Confirm holdout group logic (if we use it) is excluded from ad lists
- [ ] Confirm spend caps + alerts are set

Change log
- 2026-01-20: v0 created (A1/A3/A4 baseline)
- 2026-01-24: added enterprise/active opp suppression language based on Sales thread
- 2026-01-29: tightened A2 ‘pricing/enterprise’ audience + added consent note for EU
